narrative:
On October 9, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 42.6%, hearing 1,150 out of 2,701 scheduled cases across 65 sitting rosters. This represents a contraction compared to October 8, when the court cleared 46.1% of listed matters (1,393 of 3,021), and September 29 (49.1%), though it remains slightly higher than the 40.8% hearing rate achieved on October 7.

Roster-level performance varied markedly across benches. High throughput was led by Justice V Srishananda in Hall 23, who heard 63 of 80 listed cases (78.8%), and Justice T.P. Vivekananda in Hall 36, who processed 43 of 53 matters (81.1%). Justice R. Nataraj handled the largest individual volume, hearing 91 of 171 scheduled listings (53.2%). In contrast, full deferrals occurred on certain cause lists, including Justice M. Nagaprasanna (0 of 61 heard) and the division bench of the Chief Justice and Justice K.S. Hemalekha (0 of 17 heard), while Justice B M Shyam Prasad heard 1 of 114 matters on his primary list.

Stage-wise analysis reveals lower conversion across preliminary and procedural lists. Orders matters converted at 41.8% (410 of 982), declining from 48.1% on October 8. Admission matters converted at 46.2% (330 of 715), while Preliminary Hearings achieved 45.3% (163 of 360), down from 53.5% the previous day. Final Hearing conversion stood at 34.1% (115 of 337), slightly outpacing historical baselines from October 7 (31.5%) and September 29 (32.0%). 

By case type, Writ Petitions comprised the largest share but experienced reduced clearance at 38.6% (371 of 961), down substantially from 52.4% on October 8. Criminal Petitions converted at 42.5% (215 of 506), while Miscellaneous First Appeals improved to 40.3% (158 of 392) from 31.0% on October 8. Regular Second Appeals saw 48.6% clearance, and Criminal Appeals registered a robust 67.7% hearing rate.
